title: A Ghost for the Safehouse
premise: Kestrel Vasquez, an interpreter for a doomed peace delegation in the border city of Vellmar, has spent years surviving on translation and silence. When their handler Marek — dead for three weeks — sends them a calendar invite to a meeting that will decide who controls the delegation's stolen ceasefire ledger, Kestrel realizes someone inside their found family of fixers and guards orchestrated his death. To survive, they must trade the one secret they've kept even from themselves: that they were the one who translated the order that got Marek killed. The story ends with Kestrel burning the ledger's true copy, choosing loyalty to the living over truth for the dead, and walking out of Vellmar with the two people who chose to stay.
about_author: Coral Eriksen is a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in post-conflict regions before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose jobs are to be invisible, drawing on the languages she half-remembers and the cities she can't go back to.

chapters.title: The Packed Bag
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A routine day interpreting hostile ceasefire talks establishes the delegation's fragile world: exhausted guards, cynical fixers, and Kestrel's polished lie about being nobody important. We see the go-bag under the desk and feel the low hum of dread. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being fluent in everyone's threats but trusted by no one.

chapters.title: Invitation from a Dead Man
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At 2 a.m., a meeting request arrives from Marek's still-active account, scheduled for tomorrow at noon, location: the safehouse. Kestrel checks the morgue records; Marek is confirmed dead. Someone is using a ghost as bait. Emotional beat: cold fear sharpening into resolve — Kestrel decides to attend rather than run.

chapters.title: Everyone Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and Ilya, the delegation's head of security. Kestrel quietly tests the team for signs of betrayal while Ilya notices Kestrel lying for the first time in five years. The safehouse family dynamic — shared meals, coded check-ins — is rendered warmly, making the suspicion poisonous. Emotional beat: love curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Flashback woven with present action: the ceasefire ledger contains proof that both delegations' patrons planned the collapse of the talks — and that Marek discovered it. Kestrel recalls translating a document they now suspect was Marek's death warrant. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in shallow water.

chapters.title: Noon at the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel goes to the meeting alone and finds not Marek but Sefa, the delegation's logistics chief, waiting with a gun and an offer: hand over the ledger's location, walk away rich. Kestrel stalls, realizing Sefa couldn't have sent the invite — she thinks Marek is alive too. Emotional beat: the trap has a trap inside it.

chapters.title: Three Weeks of Lies
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya reconstructs Marek's final days through travel records and discovers the invite was sent by someone with access to the safehouse server — meaning the killer is still inside. He confronts Kestrel, demanding the truth. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other, trust rebuilt in broken pieces.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Confession
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Cornered by Ilya and the closing net, Kestrel admits what they translated and what it cost. Instead of condemnation, Ilya reveals he altered the security logs the night Marek died — to protect someone else. Emotional beat: relief and horror arriving together; the secret was never theirs alone.

chapters.title: Vellmar After Dark
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sefa's employers move up the timetable; the safehouse is compromised and the team scatters through the city's flooded undermarket. A running gunfight forces Kestrel to use every language they know to talk their way past checkpoints. Emotional beat: the found family fighting as one unit for the first time.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax. Traded to Sefa's patrons in exchange for Ilya's life, Kestrel faces the choice: reveal the ledger and doom the delegation's survivors, or die keeping it. They offer a third trade — the confession of who really ordered Marek's death — buying escape but exposing their own complicity publicly. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon aimed at oneself.

chapters.title: A Ghost for the Safehouse
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Resolution. The ledger burns; the guilty are named but unpunished, the war grinding on regardless. Kestrel, Ilya, and the youngest guard, Noor, leave Vellmar on a freight barge. Kestrel finally unpacks the go-bag. Emotional beat: survival without absolution, but with company — the first honest silence Kestrel has ever kept.
